mcqs.q: Muco-cutaneous lesions are surface lesions affecting:
mcqs.explain: Muco-cutaneous lesions involve both the mucous membranes and the skin.

mcqs.q: Herpes simplex infection belongs to which category?
mcqs.explain: Viral blistering infections such as HSV are vesiculobullous diseases.

mcqs.q: Aphthous ulcers belong to which category?
mcqs.explain: Aphthous ulcers are classified among ulcerative conditions.

mcqs.q: Lichen planus is classified as a:
mcqs.explain: Reticular lichen planus presents as white lacy striae and is grouped with white lesions.

mcqs.q: Pyogenic granuloma is classified as a:
mcqs.explain: Pyogenic granuloma is a vascular, red-blue lesion.

mcqs.q: Squamous papilloma belongs to which category?
mcqs.explain: Papillary/warty growths such as squamous papilloma are verrucal-papillary lesions.

mcqs.q: A melanotic macule belongs to which category?
mcqs.explain: Melanotic macule is a pigmented lesion.

mcqs.q: An autoimmune disease is one in which the body produces:
mcqs.explain: In autoimmune disease, antibodies are directed against self antigens.

mcqs.q: In pemphigus vulgaris, the autoantibodies target:
mcqs.explain: Anti-desmoglein-3 IgG disrupts desmosomes between keratinocytes.

mcqs.q: The antibody class responsible for pemphigus is:
mcqs.explain: Abnormal IgG binds desmoglein-3 in pemphigus vulgaris.

mcqs.q: Acantholysis refers to:
opts: Separation of epithelial cells from each other
mcqs.explain: Acantholysis = loss of intercellular (desmosomal) adhesion, producing free 'acantholytic' cells.

mcqs.q: Immunofluorescence (IFA) detects proteins in cells through:
opts: An antigen–antibody reaction with a fluorophore-labelled antibody
mcqs.explain: IFA visualises antigens via a fluorophore-labelled antibody seen under UV light.

mcqs.q: Direct immunofluorescence (DIF) is performed on:
opts: The patient's tissue with a labelled primary antibody
mcqs.explain: DIF applies a labelled primary antibody to the patient's tissue to detect bound antibody/complement in situ.

mcqs.q: Indirect immunofluorescence (IIF) detects circulating autoantibodies using:
opts: Patient serum, a substrate, and a labelled secondary antibody
A direct labelled primary antibody on tissue
mcqs.explain: IIF incubates patient serum on a substrate, then a labelled secondary antibody reveals bound autoantibodies.

mcqs.q: Immunofluorescence-labelled antibodies are visualised under:
mcqs.explain: The fluorophore emits visible light when excited by UV under a fluorescence microscope.

mcqs.q: An antibody (immunoglobulin) is composed of:
mcqs.explain: Antibodies are Y-shaped, with two heavy and two light chains (variable + constant regions).

mcqs.q: Which is a VIRAL vesiculobullous disease?
mcqs.explain: Viral causes include HSV, varicella-zoster, hand-foot-and-mouth, herpangina and measles.

mcqs.q: Which vesiculobullous disease is IMMUNOLOGIC?
mcqs.explain: Immunologic vesiculobullous diseases include pemphigus, pemphigoid, dermatitis herpetiformis and linear-IgA disease.

mcqs.q: Which vesiculobullous disease is HEREDITARY?
mcqs.explain: Epidermolysis bullosa is the hereditary blistering disease.

mcqs.q: A traumatic ulcer is classified among which ulcerative subgroup?
mcqs.explain: Traumatic ulceration is a reactive ulcerative lesion.

mcqs.q: Which is a BACTERIAL cause of oral ulceration?
mcqs.explain: Bacterial causes include tuberculosis, syphilis and actinomycosis.

mcqs.q: Erythema multiforme is classified as an ulcerative lesion that is:
mcqs.explain: Erythema multiforme is an immunologic ulcerative condition.

mcqs.q: Which neoplasm appears in the ulcerative classification?
mcqs.explain: Squamous and basal cell carcinomas can present as chronic ulcers.

mcqs.q: A persistent oral ulcer lasting more than two weeks should be:
mcqs.explain: Any non-healing ulcer >2 weeks must be biopsied to rule out malignancy.

mcqs.q: Geographic tongue is grouped with which lesions?
mcqs.explain: Geographic tongue (benign migratory glossitis) is listed among white lesions.

mcqs.q: Erythroplakia is classified as a:
mcqs.explain: Erythroplakia is a red lesion (red-blue category) with high malignant potential.

mcqs.q: Condyloma acuminatum is grouped under:
mcqs.explain: Condyloma acuminatum is a verrucal-papillary (HPV) lesion.

mcqs.q: Herpangina is classified as a:
mcqs.explain: Herpangina is a viral vesiculobullous disease (Coxsackievirus).

mcqs.q: On direct immunofluorescence, pemphigus vulgaris classically shows a:
mcqs.explain: Pemphigus shows intercellular ('fish-net') IgG deposition; pemphigoid shows a linear basement-membrane band.

mcqs.q: Identify the white, lacy reticular lesion shown.
mcqs.explain: White lacy (Wickham's) striae on the buccal mucosa are reticular lichen planus — a white lesion.

mcqs.q: Identify this shallow, painful lesion of the labial mucosa.
mcqs.explain: A round, shallow, painful ulcer with an erythematous halo is an aphthous ulcer — an ulcerative lesion.

mcqs.q: This diagram shows anti-desmoglein antibodies causing cell separation. The process is:
mcqs.explain: Autoantibodies against desmoglein break desmosomes → acantholysis (as in pemphigus).

saqs.q: Define muco-cutaneous lesions and name the six clinical categories.
saqs.a: Surface lesions of skin + mucosa. Categories: vesiculobullous, ulcerative, white, red-blue, pigmented, verrucal-papillary.

saqs.q: Outline the autoimmune mechanism of pemphigus vulgaris.
saqs.a: Abnormal IgG binds desmoglein-3 → epithelial cell separation → acantholysis (acantholytic cells).
DIF = patient tissue + labelled primary antibody (bound Ab in situ). IIF = patient serum + substrate + labelled secondary antibody (circulating autoantibodies).

saqs.q: Classify vesiculobullous diseases into three groups with one example each.
saqs.a: Viral — herpes simplex; Immunologic — pemphigus vulgaris; Hereditary — epidermolysis bullosa.

saqs.q: An oral ulcer has been present for three weeks. What is the essential next step and why?
saqs.a: Biopsy — any ulcer persisting beyond two weeks must be biopsied to exclude carcinoma.

saqs.q: Give two white lesions and two ulcerative conditions of the oral mucosa.
saqs.a: White: leukoplakia, lichen planus (or candidiasis, geographic tongue). Ulcerative: aphthous ulcer, erythema multiforme (or TB, OSCC).
